name: Soul winning & the gospel
about: Preaching the gospel to every creature.

teachings.title: Wisdom's feast and the gospel invitation
teachings.summary: Wisdom's feast pictures the gospel invitation in which Christ the bread of life calls all, simple and wise, good and bad, to come and freely take the water of life.
teachings.text:
**Proverbs 9** concludes the preface of Proverbs, the instruction of Solomon to his son on Lady Wisdom and the strange woman of folly.

Wisdom's table is set for the feast, her house ready, her wine mingled (the restoration of the preserved fruit of the vine mixed with water, spiced with myrrh, sweetened with honey), her maids sent to call all who would enter in to come.

*Whoso is simple, let him turn in hither: as for him that wanteth understanding, she saith to him, Come, eat of my bread, and drink of the wine which I have mingled.*

The unadulterated truth of God's word is that wine. The bread which has come down from heaven is Jesus.

**John 6:32-36**
*Then Jesus said unto them, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Moses gave you not that bread from heaven; but my Father giveth you the true bread from heaven. For the bread of God is he which cometh down from heaven, and giveth life unto the world. Then said they unto him, Lord, evermore give us this bread. And Jesus said unto them, I am the bread of life: he that cometh to me shall never hunger; and he that believeth on me shall never thirst. But I said unto you, That ye also have seen me, and believe not.*

Her maidens calling out to the feast of Wisdom as the parable of the wedding feast:

**Luke 14:16-23**
*Then said he unto him, A certain man made a great supper, and bade many: and sent his servant at supper time to say to them that were bidden, Come; for all things are now ready. And they all with one consent began to make excuse. The first said unto him, I have bought a piece of ground, and I must needs go and see it: I pray thee have me excused. And another said, I have bought five yoke of oxen, and I go to prove them: I pray thee have me excused. And another said, I have married a wife, and therefore I cannot come. So that servant came, and shewed his lord these things. Then the master of the house being angry said to his servant, Go out quickly into the streets and lanes of the city, and bring in hither the poor, and the maimed, and the halt, and the blind. And the servant said, Lord, it is done as thou hast commanded, and yet there is room. And the lord said unto the servant, Go out into the highways and hedges, and compel them to come in, that my house may be filled*.

Just as both the simple and the wise are compelled to turn hither to Wisdom's feast, so too the gospel is for both good and bad;

So those servants went out into the highways, and gathered together all as many as they found, both bad and good: and the wedding was furnished with guests.

**Matthew 22:10**
*So those servants went out into the highways, and gathered together all as many as they found, both bad and good: and the wedding was furnished with guests.*

Jesus crying out in the streets, telling all to come to Him;

**John 7:37-38**
*In the last day, that great day of the feast, Jesus stood and cried, saying, If any man thirst, let him come unto me, and drink. He that believeth on me, as the scripture hath said, out of his belly shall flow rivers of living water.*

Forsake the foolish and live! Whosoever will, let him come.

**Revelation 22:17**
*And the Spirit and the bride say, Come. And let him that heareth say, Come. And let him that is athirst come. And whosoever will, let him take the water of life freely*.

The invitation of God to wisdom, to knowledge and understanding, is the invitation to life; as a wedding feast laid out by the host. Where the wise enters into the meal already prepared. The wine mingled. The wedding clothes, laid out, white and pure. To eat that bread of life and drink that living water, never to hunger or thirst again.

teachings.title: Never be ashamed to preach the word
teachings.summary: As the Jews threatened the prophets and killed Christ, the world will hate Christians who preach God's word, but we must boldly share the gospel and never be ashamed of it.
teachings.text:
**John 5:14-18**
*Afterward Jesus findeth him in the temple, and said unto him, Behold, thou art made whole: sin no more, lest a worse thing come unto thee. The man departed, and told the Jews that it was Jesus, which had made him whole. And therefore did the Jews persecute Jesus, and sought to slay him, because he had done these things on the sabbath day. But Jesus answered them, My Father worketh hitherto, and I work. Therefore the Jews sought the more to kill him, because he not only had broken the sabbath, but said also that God was his Father, making himself equal with God.*

**Matthew 23:35-38**
*That upon you may come all the righteous blood shed upon the earth, from the blood of righteous Abel unto the blood of Zacharias son of Barachias, whom ye slew between the temple and the altar. Verily I say unto you, All these things shall come upon this generation. O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, thou that killest the prophets, and stonest them which are sent unto thee, how often would I have gathered thy children together, even as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings, and ye would not! Behold, your house is left unto you desolate.*

Just as the Jews frequently sought the life of Jesus, before finally killing Him on the cross, they would frequently threaten the life of the prophets, killing many.

But yet they preached the word of God. And, sometimes, they were blessed with the knowledge that the people listened and the rulers relented, and turning from their wicked ways, God repented of the evil He would do to them.

Today, worldly people who despise God and His judgment will react in the same way to Christians who preach the word of God. Who give the gospel to the lost. Who stand in the gap. Who affirm the perfect word of God in season or out of season.

But there are many who will hear His word, believe on it and repent towards God.

We cannot be afraid to share the good news. We can't hide our light under a bushel. We have to take what He has whispered in our ear and shout it from the rooftops.

And if they seek your life for it, rejoice. It is to God's glory. And if you win souls to Christ, it is to God's glory.

But never be ashamed to preach the word of God.

**Romans 1:16**
*For I am not ashamed of the gospel of Christ: for it is the power of God unto salvation to every one that believeth; to the Jew first, and also to the Greek.*

teachings.title: Don't be a Jonah
teachings.summary: The Spirit prepares hearts long before we arrive, so believers should not run from the call like Jonah but preach the gospel and lay up treasure in heaven.
teachings.text:
Given the proximity and the back and forth war, and peace and trade, many Assyrians had heard of and seen the works of the God of Israel. Many seeds were sown, and watered for this one man to bring forth this much fruit.

Long before Jonah was called, the Lord had helped create fertile ground in their hearts.

Just as Jonah had no understanding of what God had in store, and ran from the divine appointment the Lord had arranged, we have no idea the place people we meet are in. How much work has been done by the Spirit before us.

**John 16:7-11**
*Nevertheless I tell you the truth; It is expedient for you that I go away: for if I go not away, the Comforter will not come unto you; but if I depart, I will send him unto you. And when he is come, he will reprove the world of sin, and of righteousness, and of judgment: Of sin, because they believe not on me; Of righteousness, because I go to my Father, and ye see me no more; Of judgment, because the prince of this world is judged.*

The Spirit is ploughing the hearts and minds of the world. Reproving them. God's mercy is revealed from Heaven in those of us who have believed. His wrath against the ungodly. By creation itself, that men have no excuse.

But the Spirit works on them too, with the conscience given every man, to reprove sinners.

And so when Jesus says the harvest is plentiful, but the laborers few, he is talking to us.

How often are we Jonahs, running from the calling? He led an entire gentile city of Idolatry to call upon the name of the Lord. The rewards for such works are great in Heaven.

**Matthew 6:19-21**
*Lay not up for yourselves treasures upon earth, where moth and rust doth corrupt, and where thieves break through and steal: but lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust doth corrupt, and where thieves do not break through nor steal: for where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.*

How much gold, silver and precious stones do we leave by the wayside for not responding to the call like Jonah?

**1 Corinthians 3:12-15**
*Now if any man build upon this foundation gold, silver, precious stones, wood, hay, stubble; Every man's work shall be made manifest: for the day shall declare it, because it shall be revealed by fire; and the fire shall try every man's work of what sort it is. If any man's work abide which he hath built thereupon, he shall receive a reward. If any man's work shall be burned, he shall suffer loss: but he himself shall be saved; yet so as by fire.*

How can they believe if there is no preacher?

**Romans 10:14-15**
*How then shall they call on him in whom they have not believed? and how shall they believe in him of whom they have not heard? and how shall they hear without a preacher? And how shall they preach, except they be sent? as it is written, How beautiful are the feet of them that preach the gospel of peace, and bring glad tidings of good things!*

teachings.title: Bloom where the Lord has planted you
teachings.summary: Like Jeremiah, who longed to flee to the wilderness but was sent to preach at the temple gates, Christians are not to retreat to compounds but to be a light where people are, enduring tribulation with hope because Christ has overcome the world.
teachings.text:
*Oh that I had in the wilderness a lodging place of wayfaring men; that I might leave my people, and go from them! for they be all adulterers, an assembly of treacherous men.*

**Jeremiah 9** continues his prophesying, the hard preaching of the words of God against the children of Israel that remain in Judea.

And in it, the lamentation to seek to flee from Jerusalem and the wickedness of this generation, and go to the wilderness, to live off grid, and be away from the evil people, uncircumcised in the heart.

But God calls upon Jeremiah to preach in the city, by the gates of the Temple. To tell them of the pending destruction their forsaking Him has brought up on them.

This same impulse is given to Christians today. To flee the world, to get to a redoubt in the wilderness. To be far from the fallen society that, like just Lot, vexed with the filthy conversation of the wicked.

But, like the prophets, and like Christ Himself, we go to Jerusalem. We are called to go to the population centers and preach the acceptable year of the Lord. To seek that which is lost. To be a light in that darkness.

We can't be a light to others if we are hidden in the woods.

And so we are in the world, not of it.

Rather than coveting a RETVRN to a past we never knew, or a rustic compound in the hills, we are supposed to bloom where the good Lord has planted us. To be a blessing to those around us. To *be ready always to give an answer to every man that asketh you a reason of the hope that is in you with meekness and fear: having a good conscience; that, whereas they speak evil of you, as of evildoers, they may be ashamed that falsely accuse your good conversation in Christ*.

Not to flee persecution, and the tribulations that come to every believer, living for the Lord. To *glory in tribulations also: knowing that tribulation worketh patience; And patience, experience; and experience, hope: And hope maketh not ashamed; because the love of God is shed abroad in our hearts by the Holy Ghost which is given unto us.*

**James 1:12**
*Blessed is the man that endureth temptation: for when he is tried, he shall receive the crown of life, which the Lord hath promised to them that love him.*

**Romans 8:18**
*For I reckon that the sufferings of this present time are not worthy to be compared with the glory which shall be revealed in us.*

**James 1:2-4**
*My brethren, count it all joy when ye fall into divers temptations; Knowing this, that the trying of your faith worketh patience. But let patience have her perfect work, that ye may be perfect and entire, wanting nothing.*

We who believe on Christ have already overcome this fallen world. Because He has overcome death and Hell for us. We shouldn't be black pilled. We may wail with lamentations for our people to repent, but standfast in the faith that has saved us.

**John 16:33**
*These things I have spoken unto you, that in me ye might have peace. In the world ye shall have tribulation: but be of good cheer; I have overcome the world.*

teachings.title: Peace, peace, when there is no peace
teachings.summary: False prophets preach peace, prosperity and a pre-tribulation escape to itching ears, but true preachers warn of judgment and call men to repent and find peace only in Christ.
teachings.text:
**Jeremiah 6:13-15**
*For from the least of them even unto the greatest of them every one is given to covetousness; and from the prophet even unto the priest every one dealeth falsely. They have healed also the hurt of the daughter of my people slightly, saying, Peace, peace; when there is no peace. Were they ashamed when they had committed abomination? nay, they were not at all ashamed, neither could they blush: therefore they shall fall among them that fall: at the time that I visit them they shall be cast down, saith the Lord.*

**1 Thessalonians 5:1-3**
*But of the times and the seasons, brethren, ye have no need that I write unto you. For yourselves know perfectly that the day of the Lord so cometh as a thief in the night. For when they shall say, Peace and safety; then sudden destruction cometh upon them, as travail upon a woman with child; and they shall not escape.*

False prophets, claiming to speak the words of God, come with soothing words of peace. Peace with God, despite the sins of the people. Peace with the land, despite the blood of innocents. Peace with those who practice Idolatry and wickedness, in ecumenicalism.

They preach prosperity and health to people with itching ears.

**2 Timothy 4:3-4**
*For the time will come when they will not endure sound doctrine; but after their own lusts shall they heap to themselves teachers, having itching ears; and they shall turn away their ears from the truth, and shall be turned unto fables.*

Today, many false prophets also claim that believers won't see tribulation, but rather will be spared destruction, raptured before it begins.

But what does Jeremiah say to Hannah? *The prophets that have been before me and before thee of old prophesied both against many countries, and against great kingdoms, of war, and of evil, and of pestilence.*

Prophets who come with the word of God preach destruction and repentance.

And, in like manner, today we have the word of God, and we are called to do the same.

**Jude 1:22-23**
*And of some have compassion, making a difference: and others save with fear, pulling them out of the fire; hating even the garment spotted by the flesh.*

We preach the acceptable year of the Lord. That judgment is coming to every man, and Hell with it. To repent towards God and faith in His Son for deliverance. That man cannot know peace except in Christ. These are the word of God given us in scripture with the command to love one another, to set at liberty from the bonds of the law. To reconcile man with God before it's too late.

**Matthew 11:28-30**
*Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest. Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls. For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.*

teachings.title: Heap coals of fire on his head
teachings.summary: Unlike Jonah, believers must show mercy to enemies, including giving them the bread of life and water of the gospel, remembering the mercy God showed them.
teachings.text:
**Matthew 5:44-45**
*But I say unto you, Love your enemies, bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you, and pray for them which despitefully use you, and persecute you; That ye may be the children of your Father which is in heaven: for he maketh his sun to rise on the evil and on the good, and sendeth rain on the just and on the unjust.*

**Romans 9:15-16**
*For he saith to Moses, I will have mercy on whom I will have mercy, and I will have compassion on whom I will have compassion. So then it is not of him that willeth, nor of him that runneth, but of God that sheweth mercy.*

**Proverbs 25:21-23**
*If thine enemy be hungry, give him bread to eat; and if he be thirsty, give him water to drink: For thou shalt heap coals of fire upon his head, and the Lord shall reward thee. The north wind driveth away rain: so doth an angry countenance a backbiting tongue.*

Perhaps the hardest thing in the Christian life, showing mercy to those who hate us and whom we hate. But if God chooses us to be a blessing to another, it isn't on us to question why. We shouldn't be as Jonah.

And if they are hardened against us, that's on them. Our mercy will be as hot coals upon their head.

**Romans 12:20**
*Therefore if thine enemy hunger, feed him; if he thirst, give him drink: for in so doing thou shalt heap coals of fire on his head.*

Note the spiritual application of this. Your enemy hungers and thirsts. For what? Food and water? Or truth and the repentance unto faith in Christ?

Will the coals of fire make them angrier and dug in against you? Or remind them of the Hell that awaits them?

Will you withhold that bread that came down from Heaven? The waters of life that you've drank?

Are there many who don't know their right hand from left?

Only God knows.

Remember the mercy God showed you, and let that be what guides your spirit. Don't be as Jonah, and let your anger consume you.

teachings.title: The wise son and the diligent hand
teachings.summary: Proverbs contrasts the diligent, righteous and wise with the lazy fool; God provides for those who work, and the wise gather the harvest, including winning souls.
teachings.text:
**Proverbs 10** begins the more familiar listing of wise sayings, made in the Spirit by Solomon, his proverbs. But the lesson contrasting the righteous listening to instruction, being industrious, refraining from speaking evil and being wise, with the fool who is lazy, full of iniquity and violence, with a froward mouth, continues to be the primary theme carried over from the introduction in chapters 1-9.

Verse 1 contains an eternal truth that any parent could attest to. Establishing early the wisdom to found is accurate and true. A wise son is the pride of a dad, while the foolish son is the heaviness and sorrow of his mother.

From this base, the sayings stack up, precept upon precept, truth on truth. Building a foundation of wisdom that, sadly is lacking in the world today, because most, even many Christians, don't harken to the word of God. They do not fear Him, and so do not have His wisdom to rely on. They do not acknowledge Him in all their ways, and so He isn't there to direct their paths.

There are also proverbs given that have become ingrained in the secular lexicon (even if they don't acknowledge it). Such as the first half of verse 2; Gain made by wicked deeds profit nothing. In other words, crime doesn't pay. But the wise counter to this truth is that the way of the righteous delivers one from death.

We are told the truth of the Lord that He will provide for His own, the righteous won't famish, while He destroys the substance of the wicked. Not a prosperity gospel, but the understanding that when you walk in the Spirit, working in righteousness, the Lord will take care of your basic needs.

**Luke 12:27-31**
*Consider the lilies how they grow: they toil not, they spin not; and yet I say unto you, that Solomon in all his glory was not arrayed like one of these. If then God so clothe the grass, which is to day in the field, and to morrow is cast into the oven; how much more will he clothe you, O ye of little faith? And seek not ye what ye shall eat, or what ye shall drink, neither be ye of doubtful mind. For all these things do the nations of the world seek after: and your Father knoweth that ye have need of these things. But rather seek ye the kingdom of God; and all these things shall be added unto you.*

This is a promise of Christ Jesus Himself, with the caveat that the poor often are that way by being slackers, not diligent in their works.

**2 Thessalonians 3:10**
*For even when we were with you, this we commanded you, that if any would not work, neither should he eat.*

God blesses those that prepare, gathering in the summer against the winter is wise. Sleeping through the harvest is a shame. Being forward thinking and considering the end of something, understanding consequences, cause and effect, is wisdom. Shortsighted sin leads to shame.

Of course, the harvest analogy is not just applicable to agrarian cultures, or to earthly financial goals, but also the sharing of the gospel of Christ's Kingdom is frequently likened to the harvest.

**John 4:35**
*Say not ye, There are yet four months, and then cometh harvest? behold, I say unto you, Lift up your eyes, and look on the fields; for they are white already to harvest.*

Go soul-winning! The workers are few and the harvest is plenty. He that winneth souls is wise.

**Psalm 126:6**
*He that goeth forth and weepeth, bearing precious seed, shall doubtless come again with rejoicing, bringing his sheaves with him.*

But the sluggard who buries his talent of silver, to mix metaphors, he will be ashamed. He will not have sheaves of glory to rejoice in.

Being a just man, fair and merciful, extending grace to others, brings blessings and glory. The Lord will esteem the name of the just but the fool will die unknown, they will fall.

Walk upright, consider what you say. Don't be a prattling fool or a subtle and froward man, or a man of violence and offense, stirring up strifes and hatred. Knowing love covereth all sins.

**1 Peter 4:8**
*And above all things have fervent charity among yourselves: for charity shall cover the multitude of sins.*

teachings.title: Deliver them that are drawn unto death
teachings.summary: Every man is judged by his works, believers at the bema seat for reward and the lost at the Great White Throne, so a believer who fails to give the gospel to the perishing cannot plead ignorance and will suffer loss.
teachings.text:
Continuing the fatherly advice of the King, Solomon, to his son the prince,  **Proverbs 24:11-12**;

*If thou forbear to deliver them that are drawn unto death, and those that are ready to be slain; If thou sayest, Behold, we knew it not; doth not he that pondereth the heart consider it? and he that keepeth thy soul, doth not he know it? and shall not he render to every man according to his works?*

He says that failure to deliver someone marked for death by claiming ignorance to the circumstances, and potentially the injustice or false accusations that led to it, by not hearing the matter fully - that it is not an excuse. Solomon writes that we should consider our own soul, the Lord's mercy upon it, His judgment. That He will judge every man according to his works.

This is echoed in the New Testament.

**Romans 2:4-9**
*Or despisest thou the riches of his goodness and forbearance and longsuffering; not knowing that the goodness of God leadeth thee to repentance? But after thy hardness and impenitent heart treasurest up unto thyself wrath against the day of wrath and revelation of the righteous judgment of God; Who will render to every man according to his deeds: To them who by patient continuance in well doing seek for glory and honour and immortality, eternal life: But unto them that are contentious, and do not obey the truth, but obey unrighteousness, indignation and wrath, Tribulation and anguish, upon every soul of man that doeth evil, of the Jew first, and also of the Gentile*

**Hebrews 9:27**
*And as it is appointed unto men once to die, but after this the judgment.*

The wages of sin is death. We are all guilty. We will all be judged. But those in faith, who have believed on Christ, our sins not being imputed against our record, being justified by the righteousness of Jesus, our works, being built upon that foundation, are judged at the bema seat of Christ, to see what sort of works they are.

**1 Corinthians 3:12-15**
*Now if any man build upon this foundation gold, silver, precious stones, wood, hay, stubble; Every man's work shall be made manifest: for the day shall declare it, because it shall be revealed by fire; and the fire shall try every man's work of what sort it is. If any man's work abide which he hath built thereupon, he shall receive a reward. If any man's work shall be burned, he shall suffer loss: but he himself shall be saved; yet so as by fire.*

We are still saved, but, based on the criteria of God; the good will be rewarded and the vain and meaningless, destroyed.

Meanwhile, the unbelieving are judged by their works at the Great White Throne. Their works held against them;

**Revelation 20:11-15**
*And I saw a great white throne, and him that sat on it, from whose face the earth and the heaven fled away; and there was found no place for them. And I saw the dead, small and great, stand before God; and the books were opened: and another book was opened, which is the book of life: and the dead were judged out of those things which were written in the books, according to their works. And the sea gave up the dead which were in it; and death and hell delivered up the dead which were in them: and they were judged every man according to their works. And death and hell were cast into the lake of fire. This is the second death. And whosoever was not found written in the book of life was cast into the lake of fire.*

With this perspective, which Solomon clearly understood, a ruler must make the effort to know what he is judging, especially in a capital crime where a life hangs in jeopardy.

This warning applies to those that are princes by faith, in the Kingdom of God. To believers, every man we meet is appointed to death and Hell for their sins. They are drawn unto death, and ready to be slain.

If we forbear to deliver them, to give them the gospel, we cannot say we didn't know. He that pondereth the heart and keepeth our soul, He knows it. And it will be counted a loss in the trying fire at the judgment seat of Christ.

teachings.title: Wisdom maketh his face to shine
teachings.summary: Walking with God and being anointed by the Spirit changes a believer's countenance and gives boldness to preach the truth, so that others see they have been with Jesus.
teachings.text:
The Preacher continues his sermon. Having said he has searched for wisdom by observation of all things under the Sun, and having found all have sinned and fallen short. That the wise and the fool, the rich and the poor, all are appointed to die, and after this, judged and found wanting, that then the only way is God's. That fear of Him and seeking His favor is the only alternative to the vanity and vexation of spirit that man travails in.

Solomon begins **Ecclesiastes 8** praising the effect that seeking God's wisdom has on us. That it makes the face to shine, and to speak boldly His truth. That it changes the countenance of a person to walk with God.

**Exodus 34:29-30**
*And it came to pass, when Moses came down from mount Sinai with the two tables of testimony in Moses' hand, when he came down from the mount, that Moses wist not that the skin of his face shone while he talked with him. And when Aaron and all the children of Israel saw Moses, behold, the skin of his face shone; and they were afraid to come nigh him.*

Moses had to cover his face from the people, it disturbed them so much to see the radiance coming from his time with God.

**Psalm 104:15**
*And wine that maketh glad the heart of man, and oil to make his face to shine, and bread which strengtheneth man's heart*.

The Spirit is described as oil, which anoints us as we walk in Him. The bread, His word. Our heart, merry from the juice of the vine, which is Christ. He does make our faces shine. His light magnified through us, that men see us and know, we have been with Jesus. And the boldness of our wisdom comes from the confidence we have in Him and His word.

The Spirit filled the disciples of Christ, gathered in the upper room on Pentecost, and having His anointing, they went out among the multitudes gathered for the feast in Jerusalem, and preached with boldness.

Acts 2:1-4
*And when the day of Pentecost was fully come, they were all with one accord in one place. And suddenly there came a sound from heaven as of a rushing mighty wind, and it filled all the house where they were sitting. And there appeared unto them cloven tongues like as of fire, and it sat upon each of them. And they were all filled with the Holy Ghost, and began to speak with other tongues, as the Spirit gave them utterance*.

The men, hearing the miracle of preaching Christ from scripture, in their own tongues, languages from around the known world, they wondered; *Behold, are not all these which speak Galilaeans?* But the disciples had been changed by their time with God. The boldness to preach Christ from scripture, and 3,000 souls came to repentance.

Just as when Peter and John were brought before the religious leaders of the Jews for preaching Christ, these lowly fishermen gave witness that they had been with Christ by their boldness.

**Acts 4:13**
*Now when they saw the boldness of Peter and John, and perceived that they were unlearned and ignorant men, they marvelled; and they took knowledge of them, that they had been with Jesus.*

Their light so shined, that others saw and praised God. The anointing of the Spirit, the truth of God's word, the wisdom they trusted, gave them boldness to preach the truth. They were changed.

The understanding that man's countenance gives away their time with God to others, has a counterpoint in scripture. That the reprobate, those that hold the truth in unrighteousness, have a similar change;

**Isaiah 3:9**
*The shew of their countenance doth witness against them; and they declare their sin as Sodom, they hide it not. Woe unto their soul! for they have rewarded evil unto themselves.*

We should seek to walk with God, to be anointed with the Spirit, that men look upon us and take note that we have been with Jesus. To speak boldly the wisdom of the gospel. To make known the truth of His way.

teachings.title: Blessed is the man whose sin is covered
teachings.summary: As David and Paul teach, God imputes righteousness without works and does not hold the believer's sins against him, and this good news must be received today before God's Spirit ceases to strive.
teachings.text:
**Psalm 32** opens with a very familiar and important doctrine, the understanding of God's forgiveness for sin in the saved believer's life. This foundational fact is repeated by Paul in the letter to the Romans;

**Romans 4:6–8**
*Even as David also describeth the blessedness of the man, unto whom God imputeth righteousness without works, Saying, Blessed are they whose iniquities are forgiven, and whose sins are covered. Blessed is the man to whom the Lord will not impute sin.*

The truth is that, in Christ, whether it was in David's day, or Paul's or our own, God forgives our past transgressions, covers our current sin, and will not hold our future sins and iniquity against us.

This positional standing of righteousness before God, despite our sins, through His imputed righteousness is made possible, through the Holy Spirit, by the renewal, the regeneration, the quickening of our spirit. The new man within us. Blessed is the man *in whose spirit there is no guile.*

We are given the Spirit of truth, that we may acknowledge our sin, knowing that we are forgiven of all sin, first, not by works but by faith.

The same good news today as in David's day. And this Psalm serves as an evangelical appeal.

David writes of a man who kept his silence, who hadn't called upon the name of the Lord, who suffered in their sins, bones waxing old and dried up by their roaring in the daytime, the heaviness of their iniquity weighing on them at night.

But the honesty and humility of acknowledging sin, not hiding anything from God (as if we could), confessing our transgressions unto the Lord, and being forgiven, is a blessing. Rioting in the daytime and being kept up at night by our conscience, being convicted in the Spirit, gives way to the peace that passes understanding, through the forgiveness that is given to us by God's mercy and grace.

David reminds us that there is a time where God may be sought, before it is too late.

**Isaiah 55:6**
*Seek ye the LORD while he may be found, call ye upon him while he is near*

God's Spirit will not always strive with man. There comes a time when those that put off or reject the truth, not acknowledging that they are sinners, lying to God and themselves, are no longer able to come to Him. Where He no longer extends His hand, because they have hardened their hearts and will not seek Him, even as they face destruction.

**Hebrews 4:7**
*Again, he limiteth a certain day, saying in David, To day, after so long a time; as it is said, To day if ye will hear his voice, harden not your hearts.*

We have the example of those in the days of Noah, who mocked him for his faith in preparing the ark, and whose disobedient spirits who Christ preached to in Hell, were destroyed by the flood, never coming nigh unto God. Just as those left to God's wrath to come will not repent, despite the horrors of His judgment.

There is a time, it is today. There is a day, and it is the present. If you haven't accepted the truth that we are sinners in need of salvation, and that it is offered as a free gift to all who believe, through the grace of Almighty God, now is the time.

**2 Corinthians 6:2**
*(For he saith, I have heard thee in a time accepted, and in the day of salvation have I succoured thee: behold, now is the accepted time; behold, now is the day of salvation.)*

teachings.title: God shall likewise destroy thee for ever
teachings.summary: The boastful wicked who reject the fear of the Lord face eternal torment in hell, and believers should name them plainly and preach that hard truth so some may be pulled out of the fire.
teachings.text:
In **Psalm 52**, the psalmist presents the polar opposite of the contrite heart of **Psalm 51**, the mischief-making man who doesn't avail himself to the longsuffering mercy of God.

The wicked and their deceitful tongue, inventing lies, telling slander against God and God's people, boasting of their blessings, not thankful but vain in their imagination, loving evil more than good, these are the men who continually reject the call to fear the Lord.

Those of us who are saved can become incredulous at the prideful stance of the wicked, who reject the fear of God and lean on their own strength. We can often grow confounded and even depressed over the ways of the wicked. Like just Lot, living in Sodom, being afflicted by the wickedness around him

**2 Peter 2:8**
(*For that righteous man dwelling among them, in seeing and hearing, vexed his righteous soul from day to day with their unlawful deeds;)*

The Bible is not afraid to call these people out, directly and to their face. They are boastful, mockingly called "mighty men," liars, evil, haters of righteousness, lovers of slanderous and wicked words, lovers of mischief, having deceitful tongues.

We should not fear to identify exactly the perverted in our midst when they reject and mock the gospel of God and the word we preach.

Nor should we tiptoe around the heart of the matter; Their immanent destruction and the torment in the fire of Hell that awaits them.

**Jude 1:22–23**
*And of some have compassion, making a difference: And others save with fear, pulling them out of the fire; hating even the garment spotted by the flesh.*

Those who do not see the wrath of God revealed from Heaven upon others as a reason to repent and believe, and won't see the mercy and hear the praise of the meek, feeling the compassionate love of believers magnify God's grace, need hard preaching to let them know exactly what they've chosen, in hopes that they might be saved.

That their love of devouring words will lead to God likewise destroying them forever. Literally, being devoured by flame and worm in outer darkness, forever. Eternal suffering at the hands of a just and mighty God.

*God shall likewise destroy thee for ever, he shall take thee away, and pluck thee out of thy dwelling place, and root thee out of the land of the living.* *Selah*.

If "selah" is meant to be a pause, a moment to reflect on what was just sung or said, is there anywhere more fitting than in that moment, having heard that sobering truth?

God will destroy you. He will take your life and root you out of the land of the living, to place you in a place of eternal destruction.

And the righteous shall see their end and fear God, and laugh at the calamity they brought about on themselves. The end their mischief brought about, turned back upon them.

**Proverbs 26:27**
*Whoso diggeth a pit shall fall therein: and he that rolleth a stone, it will return upon him*.

The ironic nature of the bitter end experienced by the boastful sinner is often evident and clear to those that fear God. The humor of the Lord is appreciated by His children. We laugh at their calamity.

When the wicked are made a parable or a byword among the people, it should give other men pause. The wrath revealed from Heaven should give instruction to the simple to turn towards God. It shows the righteous in Christ God's power and promise.

**Proverbs 1:7**
*The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge: but fools despise wisdom and instruction.*

The warning is ignored by the fool. And God will not be mocked.

**Proverbs 1:25–30**
*But ye have set at nought all my counsel, and would none of my reproof: I also will laugh at your calamity; I will mock when your fear cometh; When your fear cometh as desolation, and your destruction cometh as a whirlwind; when distress and anguish cometh upon you. Then shall they call upon me, but I will not answer; they shall seek me early, but they shall not find me: For that they hated knowledge, and did not choose the fear of the LORD: They would none of my counsel: they despised all my reproof.*
